thread:
Aisha (docs): Heads up — I just opened a small PR to reconcile wording across the region pages. There are two spots where we say 'regional overlap' and another that implies data "storage" vs "processing" which Legal flagged. PR: https://git.redwood/example/region-terminology
Sam K: :eyes: linking now. Which pages exactly? I can patch the SDK snippet while I'm at it.
Aisha (docs): top-level 'Supported regions' landing + 'Data residency' footnote on the private deploy quickstart. The problematic sentence is: 'Data may be stored in multiple regions when overlap exists.' That reads like we store customer data in multiple places even when they selected single-region residency.
Priya (legal): Quick note from Legal: prefer precise phrasing. Suggest: 'Data processing may occur in multiple regions for routing or failover; storage will conform to the customer's selected residency when the residency option is enabled.' Also add a line about KMS/HSM: 'Encryption keys remain under customer control via KMS/HSM integrations when private residency is chosen.' :lock:
Maya R: +1 from me. Also we've had confusion over region slugs in SDK examples (eu vs eu-west-1). Can we standardize on the canonical slug we use in the control plane? That will reduce support tickets.
Jonah P: I can update the SDK snippet in the PR. Proposed python header example:

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(region="eu-west-1", api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate("Translate this to FR")
```

And a curl example:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?region=eu-west-1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

Maya R: That looks good. Also add a tiny mapping table in the doc: UI label -> canonical slug -> human-friendly name. e.g. "Europe (eu-west-1)" to avoid people using 'eu' alone.
Sam K: On the wording change: I propose we replace 'stored' with 'persisted' in the residency page and explicitly call out 'transient processing (caching, routing)'. Draft: 'Transient processing (caching, routing) may occur outside the selected residency; persisted data storage adheres to the chosen region when residency is enabled.'
Priya (legal): That sentence is fine but please add a short parenthetical: '(subject to applicable legal requests and compliance controls)'. We need that caveat for enterprise customers.
Aisha (docs): Good, I will update the PR with the legal-approved sentence and the SDK snippets from Jonah. Also adding the mapping table as a small markdown table.
Aisha (docs): @docs-ci-bot can you run the linkcheck and linter on my branch? Branch: docs/region-terminology-audit

docs-ci-bot: Running checks on docs/region-terminology-audit...

docs-ci-bot: Linkcheck: 1 broken link found -> https://old.redwood.ai/residency-whitepaper (404). Lint: passed. Spellcheck: passed.
Sam K: Ah, that's the old whitepaper link. I have the new one: https://redwood.ai/security/residency-whitepaper. I'll swap it in.
Maya R: Also consider adding an inline note for on-prem customers: 'On-prem packages perform all processing within customer-managed networks; contact sales for air-gapped installs.' Keeps expectations clear.
Aisha (docs): Will add that. Plan: I will update wording + insert SDK snippets + add mapping table + swap link + add on-prem note. After that we'll merge and ship a tiny patch release to the site.
Jonah P: I'll open a follow-up PR in case we need to change snippet variants for Dedicated vs Hosted (region flag behavior differs). Keep this PR small.
Priya (legal): Thanks — please ping me on the final diff. I'll do a quick signoff.
Aisha (docs): Thanks all :thumbsup: merging after link swap and CI green. Expected merge by EOD
